elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso permits assignment to a "successor" only; it does not permit assignment to an affiliate that is not a successor.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The proviso permits either party, including Customer, to assign to a successor upon written notice without obtaining consent; this encompasses a successor in a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The unrestricted reference to a "successor" permits Customer to assign to a successor in an acquisition upon written notice without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The unrestricted reference to a "successor" permits Customer to assign to a successor in a substantially-all-assets sale upon written notice without consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign this Agreement without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The mutual successor proviso allows Vendor to assign to a successor upon written notice without Customer's consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The retained consent provision expressly states that consent "will not be unreasonably withheld."

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: There is no competitor prohibition. Vendor may assign to a competitor with Customer consent and may assign to a competitor that is a successor upon written notice alone.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right based on Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: Neither the original language nor the rendered clause grants Vendor any termination right triggered by Customer's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor upon written notice without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso states that "either party may assign this Agreement to a successor upon written notice," which includes Customer.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor upon written notice without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso states that "either party may assign this Agreement to a successor upon written notice," which includes Vendor.

elements.element: Customer must obtain Vendor's consent for assignments other than assignments to a successor.
elements.evidence: The opening prohibition requires the other party's prior written consent, subject only to the successor proviso.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Customer assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent standard states that consent "will not be unreasonably withheld."

elements.element: Vendor must obtain Customer's consent for assignments other than assignments to a successor.
elements.evidence: The opening prohibition requires the other party's prior written consent, subject only to the successor proviso.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent standard states that consent "will not be unreasonably withheld."

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback exactly: both parties may assign to successors upon written notice, while other assignments remain subject to consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits the affiliate exception and competitor prohibition and allows Vendor to assign to a successor without Customer consent.
